newsitem.title: CHINA: Deng death wipes Korea defector off media map.
newsitem.headline: Deng death wipes Korea defector off media map.

text.p: On Wednesday, some foreign correspondents in Beijing were calling North Korea's Hwang Jang-yop the biggest story to hit the Chinese capital in years.

On Thursday, few even turned up at the police cordon around the South Korean mission to Beijing where Hwang, the most senior leader ever to flee North Korea, spent his ninth day stranded at the centre of an international diplomatic crisis.
The death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping late on Wednesday wiped Hwang off the front pages and froze attempts to thaw the diplomatic ice that has marooned him in Beijing.
"The negotiations are continuing... but we are not sure when they will start," an official of the Seoul's Bejiing mission said but declined to elaborate.

"China and South Korea share the same Asian tradition and you just don't want to disturb mourning people," a Seoul foreign ministry official told Reuters when asked about the situation of Hwang, a top aide to North Korean leader Kim Jong-il.
That could mean that Hwang may have to spend a long time in Seoul's consulate office in Beijing before a decision is reached on where he should go next.
Chinese police kept their tight cordon around the mission where Hwang was holed up, ordering away disappointed ethnic-Korean visa seekers from China's northeast provinces.
Beyond the cordon, where bleary-eyed foreign reporters had kept long vigils for days, only two Japanese television cameramen remained to monitor developments.
